note: Budgets the Nex briefing workflow enforces. Nex also enforces its own chat limits (depth 3, 8 live sub-chats per conversation); these stay below them.
scout_mode_note: topic: each scout covers one topic from categories.json (topic-scout.md). lane: each scout covers one source lane from lanes.json (source-scout.md) across categories, and media leads go to a follow-up scout. Lane mode needs lanes.json and source-scout.md; without them Nex runs topic scouts.

token_budget.note: Fresh tokens = uncached input + output, as the provider reports them per request. Best-effort: checked after each reported request and about once a minute, so a request in flight can overshoot.
token_budget.reserve_note: Held back from research for the stages every report needs. New research may start only if, with every running agent spending its whole cap plus the in-flight margin, the reserve stays untouched.
token_budget.caps_note: Scout and lead caps sit above what scouts (114k-169k) and leads (157k-255k in their first round) spent in the November 2026 test runs, so the reserve check lets four scouts run at once instead of one per lead.

gap_round.note: One bounded round after the leads hand in (references/roles/chief-editor.md, Gap round): brief.py gaps lists coverage gaps by rule, the chief decides each one (a skip needs a reason), Nex reopens the leads for the pursued ones and checks their gap_results with brief.py gap-check. reserve_fresh_tokens.gap_research is held back from the first round and released when the gap round starts.

verification.note: Independent verifiers check high-risk claims before the draft, without the author's sources (references/roles/verifier.md). Claims are chosen by brief.py verify-select.
